title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: Limits on the Number of Accounts Held
content:
A customer of Piedmont Crescent Bank may keep more than one Savings & Money Market Accounts product at the same time. Two ceilings govern how many, and both are read from the bank's own account records for that customer, never from the customer's recollection.

## Rule

1. **Across the whole family.** A new account is opened only while the customer's number of savings and money market accounts in any status other than closed is fewer than **6**.
2. **Within the tier asked for.** A new account is opened only while the customer's number of accounts of that same tier, again in any status other than closed, is fewer than the tier's own per-customer maximum. Each of the six tiers takes its ceiling from its own per-customer maximum as recorded on the tier schedule.
3. **What is counted.** An account awaiting its opening deposit, an active account and a dormant account each count toward both ceilings. A closed account counts toward neither.
4. **Outcome at a ceiling.** When either count has already reached its ceiling, the opening is declined and no account comes into existence.

## How the two counts are taken

| Count | Accounts included | Matched on | Must be |
|---|---|---|---|
| Family count | every savings or money market account of the customer that is applied, active or dormant | the customer | fewer than 6 |
| Tier count | the customer's applied, active or dormant accounts of the requested tier | the customer and the requested tier | fewer than that tier's per-customer maximum |

## Hypothetical cases

- A customer holds five accounts: two active, one dormant, one awaiting funding and one closed. The family count is four, because the closed one is left out; four is fewer than 6, so the family ceiling does not stop a new application.
- A customer holds six accounts, none closed, and asks for a seventh. The family count already stands at 6, so the opening is declined, whatever tier was requested.
- A customer's family count is three, and two of those accounts are of the tier now requested; assume, for the example, that this tier's per-customer maximum is two. Another account of that tier is declined on the tier count, even though the family count has room.

## Points of judgement

**Does a dormant account free up a place?** No. Only closure removes an account from either count.

**Is anything opened on a partial basis when a ceiling is reached?** No. The request is refused outright and nothing is created.
